document_check.note: Li W, Sun L, Yue L, Xiao S. Relationship between serum apolipoprotein B levels and depressive symptoms in elderly Chinese patients with mild cognitive impairment: a large-scale cross-sectional and five-year follow-up study. J Affect Disord 2024;344:329-334. The first author, year and cited finding match the review: only baseline MoCA predicted five-year conversion to dementia, while depressive symptoms and lipids did not.

cited_result: Five-year follow-up of 321 of the 1014 baseline MCI patients (28 converters). In Cox regression only baseline MoCA predicted conversion to dementia (HR 0.738, 95% CI 0.627-0.869; AUC 0.798). Baseline depressive-symptom severity (GDS 5.54 vs 5.73, p = 0.859), ADL and lipids did not separate converters from non-converters. The principal factor appraised is GDS depressive-symptom severity as a prognostic factor for conversion, with baseline MoCA as the contrasting factor.
tool_reason: The cited result is the association of single baseline factors (depressive-symptom severity score, MoCA) with later conversion to dementia. It is not the performance of a developed and validated multivariable model, so QUIPS fits.

domains.rationale: The source cohort and eligibility criteria are stated. Recruitment method, recruitment period and participation of eligible people are not reported; the paper refers to an earlier publication for them. People with incomplete data or who refused blood tests were excluded.

signalling.question: Is the source population and recruitment adequately described?
signalling.quote: All participants were from the Shanghai Brain Health Cohort Study, which has been described in detail in our previous study (Li et al., 2022).

signalling.question: Are inclusion and exclusion criteria adequately described?
signalling.quote: The criteria for inclusion were as follows: 1) Han Chinese; 2) aged 55 and above; 3) MCI was diagnosed by two attending physicians; 4) no previous use of psychotropic drugs or cognitive-promoting drugs.

signalling.question: Was there adequate participation in the study by eligible persons?
signalling.quote: Searched for the number approached or eligible, refusals, participation rate and recruitment dates. None are reported; details are deferred to Li et al., 2022.

signalling.question: Is the baseline study sample described for key characteristics?
signalling.quote: Among them, 330 were males, accounting for 32.6 % of the total. Their average age was 69.74 ± 8.17 years, and their average years of schooling was 9.73 ± 3.86 years.

domains.rationale: Only 321 of 1014 (32%) were followed up. There is no information on attempts to trace non-completers, and no comparison of completers with those lost. The authors themselves suggest that those lost may have progressed, which could bias the factor-outcome association in either direction.

signalling.question: Is the proportion of the baseline sample available for analysis adequate?
signalling.quote: Then we followed these 1014 MCI for five years, eventually reaching 321 of them.

signalling.question: Were attempts made to collect information on participants who dropped out?
signalling.quote: Searched for tracing, registry linkage, telephone contact or any outcome data on the 693 non-completers. None are reported.

signalling.question: Are reasons for loss to follow-up provided?
signalling.quote: the large number of people lost during the follow-up period may be the biggest limitation of our study, which is because many of those lost may have developed mild cognitive impairment or dementia, and the loss of this segment of the population may have affected the study results.

signalling.question: Are participants lost to follow-up compared with completers on key characteristics?
signalling.quote: Searched for a comparison of lost and followed participants. Table 4 describes only the 321 followed (28 MCI-to-dementia, 293 MCI-to-MCI).

domains.rationale: Depressive-symptom severity was measured at baseline with the standard 30-item GDS, using the same procedure for everyone, and was analysed as a continuous score in the follow-up comparison.

signalling.question: Is a clear definition of the prognostic factor provided?
signalling.quote: A GDS score of 10 or higher is considered to have depressive symptoms (Smarr and Keefer, 2011).

signalling.question: Is the method of measurement valid and reliable?
signalling.quote: Previous studies have shown that GDS can be applied to elderly people in the community with high sensitivity and specificity (Liu et al., 2021; Huang et al., 2021).

signalling.question: Were the same method and setting used for all participants?
signalling.quote: Meanwhile, they also completed a series of scale assessments, including Geriatric depression scale (GDS), Ability of Daily Living (ADL), Montreal cognitive assessment (MoCA) and Block Design Test (BDT).

signalling.question: Is the continuous factor reported, or are appropriate cut-points used?
signalling.quote: GDS 5.54 ± 6.18 5.73 ± 5.46 0.032 0.859 (Table 4, MCI-to-dementia vs MCI-to-MCI)

domains.rationale: Dementia was defined by DSM-IV, and follow-up procedures matched baseline. Blinding of outcome assessors to baseline data is not reported. The outcome was ascertained at a single follow-up visit without event dates, and the dementia diagnosis relies on the same cognitive testing that yields MoCA, so the MoCA contrast is prone to incorporation.

signalling.question: Is a clear definition of the outcome provided?
signalling.quote: The diagnosis of dementia was based on the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of mental disorders, Fourth Edition (DSM-IV)

signalling.question: Was the same method used to measure the outcome in all participants?
signalling.quote: The study procedures for follow-up assessment were consistent with baseline, but lipid markers were not repeated.

signalling.question: Was the outcome assessed without knowledge of the baseline prognostic factor?
signalling.quote: Searched for blind, masked, unaware or independent assessment of dementia status. None is reported.

signalling.question: Was the timing of outcome ascertainment appropriate?
signalling.quote: with conversion to dementia as the dependent variable and the difference between baseline survey time and follow-up survey time as the time variable

domains.rationale: The covariate rule is defined only for the cross-sectional analysis. For the follow-up, the Cox model entered 'baseline variance variables' without naming an adjustment set, and the null finding for GDS rests on an unadjusted comparison, although converters were nine years older and less educated.

signalling.question: Were important potential confounders measured?
signalling.quote: General demographic information, including age, gender, education, height and weight were collected by a standardized questionnaire.

signalling.question: Were confounders accounted for in the design or analysis of the factor-outcome association?
signalling.quote: Those variables that differed between MCI with depressive symptoms and MCI without depressive symptoms groups were considered as covariates. ... Then Cox regression analysis was used to investigate the association between baseline variance variables and future cognitive outcomes

signalling.question: Do converters and non-converters differ on important confounders?

domains.rationale: With 28 events, the variables were screened by univariable group differences, and Table 5 reports only the significant MoCA row. No estimate is reported for GDS, ADL or lipids, and GDS (which did not differ univariably) appears not to have been entered. The AUC is apparent performance with no validation. Selective reporting is likely.

signalling.question: Is there sufficient presentation of data to assess the adequacy of the analysis?
signalling.quote: Results of COX regression analysis suggest that baseline MoCA scores could predict the risk of MCI developing dementia. ... MoCA −0.304 0.083 13.271 1 <0.001* 0.738 0.627–0.869

signalling.question: Is the model-building strategy appropriate, with adequate events?
signalling.quote: Of the 321 patients who were eventually followed up, 28 developed dementia and 293 maintained their cognitive status.

signalling.question: Is there no selective reporting of results?
signalling.quote: The results of Cox regression analysis showed that only baseline MoCA scores could predict the risk of future MCI transition to dementia (p < 0.001, HR = 0.738, 95 % confidence interval: 0.627–0.869).

overall: High risk of bias (QUIPS: attrition, confounding, and statistical analysis and reporting high; participation and outcome measurement moderate; prognostic factor measurement low).
overall_rationale: Three domains are high. 68% of the baseline sample was lost without comparison, the GDS null finding rests on an unadjusted comparison, and with only 28 events the Cox model reports only the significant MoCA row. Any high domain makes the overall rating high.

applicability.rationale: The sample is untreated Han Chinese community MCI aged 55 and over, diagnosed clinically without MRI and without subtyping. The authors acknowledge that this may introduce diagnostic error.
